title: Passing events safely from an ISR

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Passing events safely from an ISR”?
options: Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
A queue moves the event to a task, which can do longer work without blocking interrupts.
questions.answer: A queue moves the event to a task, which can do longer work without blocking interrupts.
questions.explanation:
A queue moves the event to a task, which can do longer work without blocking interrupts.
Why: An interrupt service routine (ISR) reacts to hardware events and should do only short, non-blocking work. FreeRTOS `FromISR` APIs can send a queue item or notification; move sensor reads, logging, and protocol work to a task. The correct ISR API, IRAM placement, and pin interrupt support depend on the target and board.
